prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a layered layout: the bed occupies the near left foreground at roughly 0.3–1 m, the chair/rail and occasional lower-edge objects are about 0.7–1.5 m away, the TV and cabinet are approximately 1.5–2.5 m ahead-left, and the standing person is roughly 2–3 m ahead-right near the doorway. The person is around 1–2 m to the right of the TV and behind the chair/rail; the rear wall and windows are farther away, while the bright bed edge is the nearest large surface and partly leaves the frame. Across the five frames, lateral shifts and changing apparent sizes mainly show the camera turning or translating: the TV and person move across the image, but neither displays a clear sustained approach or retreat, and the person remains oriented mostly sideways rather than toward the camera. Compared with RGB, the map makes foreground-versus-background separation and occlusion order much clearer, but its grayscale is not metrically calibrated, object boundaries bleed together, and the very dark ceiling/wall regions and bright bed surfaces make precise distances unreliable.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map identifies a person ahead-right, a TV ahead-left, the bed entering from the left foreground, a chair at the lower right in later frames, and a suitcase-like object near the lower centre in the middle frames. These masks clarify which overlapping regions belong to separate objects: the bed is nearer and left of the TV, the person stands right of the TV and behind the chair, and the suitcase is low in front of or near the person; approximate distances from RGB context are about 0.3–1 m for the bed, 0.7–1.5 m for the chair/suitcase, 1.5–2.5 m for the TV, and 2–3 m for the person. Over the sequence, all masks shift laterally with the egocentric camera motion; the chair and suitcase enter or leave the cropped lower edge, while the person remains largely side-on and shows no clear turn toward the camera wearer. The map reveals object extents and partial occlusions more clearly than RGB, but it omits much of the room, changes mask colours between frames, inconsistently detects the chair and suitcase, and clips objects that extend beyond the image.
descriptions.pose: The pose map isolates one standing person roughly 2–3 m ahead-right, with the torso upright, one arm bent forward around chest or waist height, and the head angled mostly sideways rather than directly toward the camera wearer. The skeleton shows the person's limb configuration more clearly than RGB and indicates that the hands are close to the person's own torso and within that person's arm's reach, while no mapped body part is within the camera wearer's arm's reach. Across the five frames, the skeleton shifts right-left with camera motion and becomes slightly smaller in some frames, but there is no reliable sustained approach, retreat, or full-body turn; the relative pose remains broadly stable. The map gives little direct room layout or object distance information, the legs and feet are incomplete or merged, hand detections are sparse or absent, and several joints appear displaced, so exact facing direction, gaze, and contact with nearby objects are uncertain.
